### Fact sheet

**Hypothesis (Goal):** a single shift-direction + cosine-scaled magnitude (rank-one) governs cross-context generalization for the marker implant and breaks for the EM implant.

**Verdict: the ordering came out reversed, and the magnitude half holds in neither arm.** All numbers from `eval_results/issue_521/svd/headline_metrics.json` + per-cell JSONs (primary read = trained-model-text variant, layer 14, 14 personas × 20 held-out questions, 3 seeds/arm).

- **Direction concentration (top singular share, σ1/Σσ):** marker 0.325/0.311/0.348 (row-shuffle null p95 0.197/0.213/0.187); EM 0.524/0.572/0.603 (row-shuffle p95 0.494/0.540/0.575; sign-flip p95 0.083-0.086). All six cells > both nulls' p99 (empirical p < 0.01, 1,000 reps). EM > marker in every seed pairing and under all 3 measurement variants. Note: the row-shuffle null is conservative for near-parallel columns (it preserves the common component), so the small EM observed-minus-null margin understates EM structure; the sign-flip null is the cleaner EM floor.
- **Per-persona alignment to the top direction (mean cos):** EM 0.963/0.974/0.980 — every persona ~parallel to one direction. Marker 0.587/0.713/0.550 with BIMODAL structure: stable high cluster (software_engineer, police_officer, data_scientist, librarian: 0.73-0.98 in all seeds) vs the rest at 0.24-0.49. The trained source (medical_doctor) is the LOWEST in all 3 seeds (0.318/0.302/0.241) — the marker arm's shared direction is a bystander direction.
